_doc: Cybernetic organization theory mapped onto the managers and staff a system runs. The exact text 'Organizational Theory: A Cybernetic Approach' could not be located (2026-11-27 searches), so the map uses the closest primary sources: Stafford Beer's Viable System Model (Brain of the Firm, 1972) and Ashby's law of requisite variety (An Introduction to Cybernetics, 1956). Summaries are ours; sources are linked. Every function names the roles that carry it (each a switched-on manager in seed/autonomy/managers.json) and the code that does the work. Checked by python3 -m foundation orgcyber --check.

functions.summary: The units that do the actual work; each is itself a viable system.
Damps oscillation between operating units so they do not fight over the same thing.
Allocates resources across the units and holds them to account here and now.
Direct, sporadic audit of the units, bypassing their own reports.
Looks outside and ahead: the environment, competitors, what to become next.
Identity and policy; balances present control against future intelligence.
An alarm that skips the normal hierarchy when something goes badly wrong.
Filters incoming variety so a regulator is not swamped.
Multiplies a regulator's own variety so it can match what it faces.
Every viable system contains, and is contained in, viable systems of the same shape.
